backlog.title: Config Layer Bug Fixes
backlog.description: Fix the two bugs found during end-to-end PRD validation: BUG-001 (major) where config init --force injects an inconsistent [role.stager] provider that breaks multi-commit decomposition, and BUG-002 (minor) where the newer-than-binary config version notice suggests the destructive config init --force. Both fixes are surgical edits to the config layer (internal/cmd/config.go, internal/config/load.go) with no structural architecture changes.

milestones.title: Fix config init --force and version-notice bugs
milestones.description: Two independent bug fixes in the config layer: (1) re-target the config init --force template to the preserved [defaults] provider instead of auto-detecting pi, and (2) drop the destructive config init --force suggestion from the newer-than-binary version advisory. Both are low-risk surgical changes with regression tests.

tasks.title: Fix BUG-001: config init --force re-targets template to preserved provider
tasks.description: When config init --force runs without --provider, GenerateBootstrapConfig("") auto-detects pi and writes an ACTIVE [role.stager] provider = "pi" block. MergeActiveSettings then preserves the user's [defaults] provider = "claude" but cannot reconcile the stager block (which exists only in the fresh template). The result is internally inconsistent: stager routes to pi but model falls back to the global "sonnet" — hitting the FR-R5b hard error on decompose. Fix: read the existing file's active [defaults] provider BEFORE calling GenerateBootstrapConfig, validate it against the built-in registry, and pass it through so the template is generated for the correct provider.

subtasks.title: Add preservedDefaultProvider helper to extract validated provider from existing config
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/018_29b859efcd56/bugfix/001_4be1bd5c953f/architecture/bug001_analysis.md for the full root-cause trace. ActiveSettings (internal/config/inert.go:38) returns section→key→raw value maps where values are stored VERBATIM (not unquoted): `provider = "claude"` → key "provider", value `"claude"` (WITH surrounding quotes). The built-in registry is `provider.NewRegistry(nil)` (built-ins only); `reg.Get(name)` returns `(*Manifest, bool)`.
2. INPUT: A file path `string` pointing at an existing config file on disk. No other inputs.
3. LOGIC: Implement a function `preservedDefaultProvider(path string) string` in internal/cmd/config.go that: (a) reads the file at path via os.ReadFile; on error returns "". (b) Calls `config.ActiveSettings(string(data))` and looks up section "defaults" → key "provider". If absent returns "". (c) Strips surrounding TOML double-quotes from the value via `strings.Trim(v, "\"")` — ActiveSettings stores values verbatim. (d) Validates the unquoted provider name against the built-in registry: `reg := provider.NewRegistry(nil); _, ok := reg.Get(v)`. If NOT a known built-in, returns "" (fall back to auto-detection — do not break custom/unknown providers). (e) Returns the validated provider name. Mock: none — this function only does file I/O and registry lookup; no external services to mock. The registry is always built-ins-only (nil arg).
4. OUTPUT: Returns a Go `string` — a validated built-in provider name (e.g. "claude"), or "" to signal fall-back to auto-detection. Consumed by Subtask P1.M1.T1.S2 which passes it to config.GenerateBootstrapConfig.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add a Go doc comment on the function explaining the BUG-001 rationale (re-target template to preserved provider instead of auto-detecting pi), referencing FR-B2/FR-B8. No external doc file changes in this subtask.

subtasks.title: Wire preservedDefaultProvider into runConfigInit so --force re-targets the template
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/018_29b859efcd56/bugfix/001_4be1bd5c953f/architecture/bug001_analysis.md. The current runConfigInit (internal/cmd/config.go:459) reads the --force flag AFTER calling GenerateBootstrapConfig. The fix requires moving the --force flag read UP before the provider generation block. The existing --provider validation block (config.go:472-479) validates non-empty providerName against the registry — this still works correctly when providerName is populated by preservedDefaultProvider because it only returns known built-ins. The --template and --interactive paths are NOT affected (they branch before the provider logic).
2. INPUT: Function `preservedDefaultProvider(path string) string` from Subtask P1.M1.T1.S1. The `path` variable is `config.ResolveConfigPath(flagConfig)` (already computed in runConfigInit). The `force` bool from `cmd.Flags().GetBool("force")`.
3. LOGIC: In runConfigInit (internal/cmd/config.go): (a) Move the `force, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("force")` line from its current position (after GenerateBootstrapConfig) to just BEFORE the `if tmpl { ... } else { ... }` block. (b) Inside the `else` branch (populated config path), after reading `providerName` from the --provider flag but BEFORE the validation block, add: `if force && providerName == "" { providerName = preservedDefaultProvider(path) }`. This ensures: --force without --provider → use preserved provider; --force with --provider → --provider wins; no --force → auto-detect unchanged. (c) The existing validation block `if providerName != "" { reg.Get(providerName) ... }` then validates the preserved provider (always a known built-in by construction) — no change needed. (d) The MergeActiveSettings call later in the function now receives a fresh template generated for the CORRECT provider, so [role.stager] is already consistent and the merge is clean. Mock: none — this is an integration edit in the command handler. Test by running the real command via Execute(context.Background()).
4. OUTPUT: Modified runConfigInit that produces an internally-consistent config on `config init --force` without `--provider`. The [role.stager] block either inherits the preserved provider (for stager-capable providers like claude) or is explicitly routed correctly — never to an inconsistent pi when the default is claude.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the Go comment block on runConfigInit (config.go:456-458) to document the BUG-001 re-targeting behavior: '--force re-targets the template to the preserved [defaults] provider instead of auto-detecting pi (BUG-001), so the generated [role.*] blocks are structurally consistent with the preserved default.' No external doc file changes here — changeset-level docs are in P1.M1.T3.

tasks.title: Fix BUG-002: newer-than-binary version notice drops destructive config init --force
tasks.description: The default (version > CurrentConfigVersion) branch of configVersionNotice in load.go:642-644 suggests 'run config init --force to regenerate', which contradicts FR-B4 and would regenerate the user's newer config at the old binary's schema version — effectively destroying it. Fix: drop the 'config init --force' clause from the newer branch so it advises only 'Upgrade stagecoach'. Also harden the dead older/missing branches for defense-in-depth.

subtasks.title: Fix configVersionNotice newer branch + harden dead branches + update tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/018_29b859efcd56/bugfix/001_4be1bd5c953f/architecture/bug002_analysis.md. The function `configVersionNotice(fileLoaded bool, version int) string` is at internal/config/load.go:629. It has 4 switch cases: version==current (returns ""), version==0, version<current, default (>current). In Load() (load.go:192-201), the migration branch handles version<current and version==0 BEFORE configVersionNotice is called — so only the default (>current) branch is LIVE. The test is at load_test.go:1962 (TestConfigVersionNotice, table-driven).
2. INPUT: No external inputs — this subtask edits the existing pure function and its table-driven test.
3. LOGIC: (a) FIX THE LIVE BRANCH (load.go:642-644): Change the default branch format string from `"Upgrade stagecoach, or run 'stagecoach config init --force' to regenerate.\n"` to `"Upgrade stagecoach.\n"` — matching FR-B4 ('the remedy is to upgrade stagecoach'). (b) DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH ON DEAD BRANCHES (load.go:636-641): In the version==0 branch, change the suggestion from `"Run 'stagecoach config upgrade' or 'stagecoach config init --force'.\n"` to `"Run 'stagecoach config upgrade'.\n"`. In the version<current branch, make the same change. These branches are dead code today (migration handles them) but could become live if the migration branch is refactored. (c) UPDATE TESTS (load_test.go:1962-2004): Change the 'ahead (4)' test case contains list from `["schema version 4", "supports up to 3", "config init --force"]` to `["schema version 4", "supports up to 3", "Upgrade stagecoach"]` and add a NOT-contains assertion that the result does NOT contain "config init --force". For the 'missing (0)' and 'older (1)' test cases, remove "config init --force" from the contains lists (replace with just "config upgrade"). (d) Update the Go doc comment on configVersionNotice (load.go:625-628) to note that per FR-B4 the newer-than-binary remedy is upgrade-only and the older/missing branches advise config upgrade (not config init --force). Mock: none — configVersionNotice is a pure function with no I/O.
4. OUTPUT: configVersionNotice returns advisory text that NEVER suggests config init --force for any version-mismatch case. The newer-than-binary case advises only 'Upgrade stagecoach'. Tests assert the absence of 'config init --force' in all non-empty branches.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the Go doc comment on configVersionNotice to reference FR-B4 rationale. No external doc file changes here — changeset-level docs are in P1.M1.T3.
